subject: Emotions
title: Tears of Joy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tears of Joy usable.

hook.text: A soldier returns home and his dog leaps into his arms. He cries. Why does extreme joy produce the same tears as grief?

buildup.text: Psychologist Oriana Aragon found that crying during joy helps regulate overwhelming positive emotions.

discovery.text: The brain uses the same release valve for both extremes. Tears restore balance after any emotional overload.

twist.text: This is why we pinch cute babies' cheeks or squeeze adorable puppies. Aggressive acts balance extreme positive feelings.

climax.text: Aragon calls it 'dimorphous expression'—using an opposite emotion to regulate an overwhelming one.

punchline.text: Crying from joy means the feeling was too big to hold.

quiz.question: What is 'dimorphous expression'?
options: Using opposite emotions to regulate strong feelings
